audit.whatIsWrong: win[] and phases[].side gave Gwen neither item stage and contradicted whys[0], whys[3], whys[5] and whys[6].
audit.why: Mini-Gnar's Boomerang Throw and Hop out-range and out-kite a 450 cone with no mist and no dash; levels 4-5 are the one coinflip once Skip 'n Slash is online; Gwen only takes over at two items, which whys[6] states.
audit.corrected: Gnar / Gnar / Gnar / Skill / Gnar / Gnar / Gwen.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns given, so 'punish a whiffed boomerang' and 'never commit while he is one boomerang from mega' have no timing attached.
audit.why: Boomerang Throw 16/14.5/13/11.5/10, Hop 22/19.5/17/14.5/12, W (Hyper/Wallop) a flat 7s and GNAR! 90/60/30, against Skip 'n Slash at 13s and Hallowed Mist at 22s. A 22-second Hop is the real gap-closing window; a 7-second Wallop is why you cannot simply outlast the stun.
audit.corrected: mid, whys[3] and spikes[1].text now carry the numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page says catching his boomerang 'lowers its cooldown for him' but never draws the consequence, and never states that Hallowed Mist does not stop a stun that is already travelling.
audit.why: Boomerang Throw refunds cooldown when he catches it, so trading into the return path funds his next poke. And Hallowed Mist stops Gnar TARGETING you from outside it - it does not delete a Wallop line already in flight or a GNAR! knockup mid-air, which is why the mist has to be down before the transform animation resolves rather than after.
audit.corrected: early and mid now state that the mist must precede the cast, not answer it.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your first breath: you finally have a real kit and can use Skip 'n Slash to dash in, snip, and reset the dash off the cooldown refund when you hit him, so you can contest a CS or punish a whiffed boomerang. But level 6 swings back to him: the moment his Rage fills, mega-Gnar's Wallop line-stun can pin you the instant you leave your mist, and GNAR! can throw you into a wall for a longer stun — either one chains into his beefier autos for a free kill or a gank setup. The whole mid game is a Rage-bar reading exercise — drop Hallowed Mist as the transform animation starts so the stun follow-up whiffs, and never commit while he is one boomerang from going mega.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your first breath: you finally have a real kit and can use Skip 'n Slash to dash in, snip, and refund the dash off hitting him, so a whiffed Hop is a 22-second window at rank 1 to actually reach him. But level 6 swings back: the moment his Rage fills, mega-Gnar's Wallop line-stun can pin you the instant you leave your mist, and GNAR! can throw you into a wall for longer — either chains into his beefier autos. Wallop is a flat 7s, three times faster than your Mist, so you cannot outlast it; drop Hallowed Mist as the transform animation starts, before the stun is in flight, and never commit while he is one boomerang from mega.

edits.before: Gnar owns the first three levels and you cannot fight it honestly. Mini-Gnar's boomerang (Q) and Hop (E) let him poke and reposition while your only tool is a slow six-snip cone you can barely land on a target that keeps hopping away, and you have no W mist for safety or E dash to close yet. Do not walk up to throw a Q he just kites out of. Soak XP at max range, eat the chip, and watch his Rage bar climb rather than his health bar — catching his boomerang lowers its cooldown for him, so chasing trades into it only feeds his poke. Track the Rage, not the HP.
edits.after: Gnar owns the first three levels and you cannot fight it honestly. Mini-Gnar's Boomerang Throw (Q) and Hop (E) let him poke and reposition while your only tool is a slow six-snip cone you can barely land on a target that keeps hopping away, and you have no W mist or E dash yet. Do not walk up to throw a Q he kites out of. Soak XP at max range, eat the chip, and watch his Rage bar rather than his health bar — catching his boomerang refunds its cooldown, so trading into the return path only funds his next poke. Track the Rage, not the HP.

edits.before: Your Skip 'n Slash dash-and-reset finally lets you contest, but you're a melee with no W up yet against a ranged kiter, so the window is a coinflip.
edits.after: Skip 'n Slash finally lets you contest and a whiffed 22s Hop is a real window, but you are a melee with no W up yet against a ranged kiter — coinflip.

edits.before: When his Rage bar fills, mega-Gnar's Wallop line-stun (and GNAR! into a wall) pins you the instant you step out of Hallowed Mist, setting up his burst or a jungle gank.
edits.after: When Rage fills, mega-Gnar's Wallop line-stun — a flat 7s, far faster than your Mist — pins you the instant you step out, and GNAR! into a wall is longer, setting up a gank.

edits.before: Bait the mega transform, drop W as Wallop lands, then R-slow and grind him out in the extended brawl where your sustain wins
edits.after: Bait the mega transform and drop W before Wallop is in flight, then R-slow and grind him out in the extended brawl your sustain wins

notes: This page's ability names are all correct, including the mega-form names Wallop and GNAR!, and the prose is second-person. Two fixes. (1) The chart gave Gwen nothing and Gnar only four stages while calling levels 1, 4-5 and 6 even or Gnar's in the wrong places - it disagreed with the whys at levels 1, 4-5 and both item stages. whys[0] says mini-Gnar out-ranges and out-kites you at 1; whys[3] calls 4-5 a coinflip; whys[6] says two items in you shred him. Corrected to Gnar/Gnar/Gnar/Skill/Gnar/Gnar/Gwen. (2) No cooldowns anywhere on a page whose entire mid-game instruction is 'read the Rage bar and drop W on the transform'. The two numbers that matter: Hop/Crunch is 22s at rank 1, so a whiffed Hop is a genuine 22-second window to close on him, and Wallop shares the W slot's flat 7s cooldown, so the mega stun comes back roughly three times faster than your Hallowed Mist does - which is why the page's advice to 'walk fights into your mist' cannot mean waiting out the stun.
